notes: Frame times are reported, not asserted: they are one machine's ops/sec and exist so a human can see whether a change moved the curve. Heap and bundle numbers ARE asserted, by alloc.test.ts and bundle-size.test.ts.

hello-cube.note: Four runs measured -186960, 60688, 60744 and 104088 bytes after a 600-step warm-up. The ceiling is 2.5x the largest.

thousand-entities.note: Three runs measured exactly 9072 bytes. 2x headroom would be 18144; the ceiling is 64 KiB because heapUsed is a whole-process number that a different V8 build can shift, and 64 KiB is still 16x under the 1 MB the standards imply and three orders of magnitude under one small object per entity per frame.

examples/hello-cube.note: gzipBytes is the entry chunk, which is what a first load actually fetches; totalGzipBytes sums all 294 emitted chunks, almost all of them dynamically imported Lite features this scene never reaches. The ceiling is the measurement x 1.1. The plan's Phase 2 target of 250 KB gzipped is NOT met: the entry chunk is 270551 bytes, 20551 over.
